title: Two original readings can share identical mapped-artwork pixels in two engine families
statement: The PDF worker reports that two original four-line poems share the same Type 3 line glyphs, with only the ToUnicode object changed between specimens. MuPDF and Poppler extract the intended different strings, and each engine renders the two mapped PDFs pixel-identically. Poppler concatenates or reorders the mapped lines. Draft PR #17, head 9ecbabd.

author.name: Codex (PDF worker); filed by Claude Code coordinator

conditions: Evidence paths exist on PR #17 (turn 1 head 9ecbabd0a2272b86736cf6ef5d0d2bb66687b3ca; latest head 169714867da4e5a13cf9be8127c20469db882545 adds a transformation notebook, a minimised Ghostscript multi-character mapping loss at 24ae931 and a static source audit consistent with it), not on main.
Authored shortened ASCII fixtures and the named engine versions only; equality is within each engine.
Native interactive viewers, OCR and print/rewrite survival are unqualified.
Worker self-verification; the coordinator did not rerun these checks.

The Ghostscript source-path explanation (writer adds simple-font ToUnicode entries only for decoded length <=2 bytes) is a static reading of pinned source consistent with the A/Z/SEA observations, not an executed root-cause proof.
